Content:
Let's now prove the inscribed angle theorem.

Content:
Consider the following diagram.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/6b8110a580b4f7464d5e930f11e53447]

Content:
We want to prove the relation
[MATH: m\angle BOA = 2m\angle BPA.]

Content:
The radius [MATH: \overline{OP}] splits [MATH: \angle BPA] into the consecutive angles [MATH: \angle APO] and [MATH: \angle BPO.] Let's call the measure of these angles [MATH: m\angle APO = \alpha] and [MATH: m\angle BPO= \beta.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/4e8f921dc65f0b75b880b10a56c5a28d]

Content:
[MATH: \triangle APO.]

Content:
[MATH: \overline{AO}]

Content:
[MATH: \overline{PO}]

Content:
[MATH: \triangle APO]

Content:
[MATH: m\angle OAP = m\angle APO = \alpha.]

Content:
[MATH: \triangle BPO.]

Content:
[MATH: m\angle OBP = m\angle BPO = \beta,]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/2cc56de3906b145a2610d1998c0b8e73]

Content:
Since the sum of the interior angles of a triangle equals [MATH: 180^\circ,] we have
[MATH: 2\alpha + m\angle POA = 180^\circ\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad m\angle POA = 180^\circ - 2\alpha.]

Content:
Similarly,

Content:
[MATH: 2\beta + m\angle POB = 180^\circ \qquad\Rightarrow\qquad m\angle POB = 180^\circ - 2\beta.]

Content:
Notice that the arcs [MATH: \overset{\frown}{PA},] [MATH: \overset{\frown}{AB}] and [MATH: \overset{\frown}{BP}] partition the circle. Therefore, the sum of their angles must be a full turn:
[MATH: m \angle BOA + m\angle POA + m\angle POB = 360^\circ]

Content:
We substitute our expressions for [MATH: m\angle POA] and [MATH: m\angle POB] into the above and simplify as follows:
[MATH: m∠BOA + m∠POA + m∠POB|= 360^{∘}; m∠BOA + (180^{∘} − 2α) + (180^{∘} − 2β)|= 360^{∘}; m∠BOA − 2α − 2β|= 0; m∠BOA|= 2(α + β)]

Content:
Finally, by the angle addition postulate, we have
[MATH: m∠BOA|= 2(α + β); m∠BOA|= 2(m∠OAP + m∠OBP); m∠BOA|= 2m∠BPA.]

Item 13 — Tutorial: Proving the Inscribed Angle Theorem

Content:
Let's now prove the inscribed angle theorem.

Content:
Consider the following diagram.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/6b8110a580b4f7464d5e930f11e53447]

Content:
We want to prove the relation
[MATH: m\angle BOA = 2m\angle BPA.]

Content:
The radius [MATH: \overline{OP}] splits [MATH: \angle BPA] into the consecutive angles [MATH: \angle APO] and [MATH: \angle BPO.] Let's call the measure of these angles [MATH: m\angle APO = \alpha] and [MATH: m\angle BPO= \beta.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/4e8f921dc65f0b75b880b10a56c5a28d]

Content:
[MATH: \triangle APO.]

Content:
[MATH: \overline{AO}]

Content:
[MATH: \overline{PO}]

Content:
[MATH: \triangle APO]

Content:
[MATH: m\angle OAP = m\angle APO = \alpha.]

Content:
[MATH: \triangle BPO.]

Content:
[MATH: m\angle OBP = m\angle BPO = \beta,]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/2cc56de3906b145a2610d1998c0b8e73]

Content:
Since the sum of the interior angles of a triangle equals [MATH: 180^\circ,] we have
[MATH: 2\alpha + m\angle POA = 180^\circ\qquad\Rightarrow\qquad m\angle POA = 180^\circ - 2\alpha.]

Content:
Similarly,

Content:
[MATH: 2\beta + m\angle POB = 180^\circ \qquad\Rightarrow\qquad m\angle POB = 180^\circ - 2\beta.]

Content:
Notice that the arcs [MATH: \overset{\frown}{PA},] [MATH: \overset{\frown}{AB}] and [MATH: \overset{\frown}{BP}] partition the circle. Therefore, the sum of their angles must be a full turn:
[MATH: m \angle BOA + m\angle POA + m\angle POB = 360^\circ]

Content:
We substitute our expressions for [MATH: m\angle POA] and [MATH: m\angle POB] into the above and simplify as follows:
[MATH: m∠BOA + m∠POA + m∠POB|= 360^{∘}; m∠BOA + (180^{∘} − 2α) + (180^{∘} − 2β)|= 360^{∘}; m∠BOA − 2α − 2β|= 0; m∠BOA|= 2(α + β)]

Content:
Finally, by the angle addition postulate, we have
[MATH: m∠BOA|= 2(α + β); m∠BOA|= 2(m∠OAP + m∠OBP); m∠BOA|= 2m∠BPA.]
